shadow:
An itch lives under the skin of a good life. The day went fine, the meal was eaten, the work got done, and still something is not quite landing. It has no clear cause. It is not grief, not boredom, not worry. It is the feeling that the real thing is somewhere up ahead, a little out of reach, and that you would have it already if you had only made a different turn.

Most people read this as a problem to solve. So the solving begins. A new plan, a better routine, a course, a move, a different version of yourself. None of them stop the itch for long, because it is not waiting on the next thing. It is waiting on a future that does not exist yet and never quite arrives.

Here is the part that is easy to miss. The itch is not a fault. It is the life force pressing, the same pressure that built every road and every cure. It points outward only because nobody told it the joy it is hunting was never out there. It is just aimed at the wrong horizon, and it will keep aiming there until the chase wears itself down.
repressive: Almost nobody can bank this fire down. The life force will not be sat on. The rare attempt to deaden it, to call the flatness peace and stop wanting anything at all, does not hold. The wanting leaks back.
reactive: More often it spills outward as meddling. Hands that cannot leave things alone, fixing what was not broken, steering other people's lives, rearranging the room. The interference scratches the itch for a second, then makes more of it.
gift:
The chase tires itself out and a quiet gives way inside it. Not a decision, more like the moment you stop pulling a knot and feel it loosen on its own. The energy that was straining toward some better tomorrow has nowhere left to run. So it turns around and floods back inward.

What comes back is vitality. Plain aliveness, the kind that does not need a reason. The body feels less like a thing being driven somewhere and more like a place that is lit. You catch yourself glad in the middle of an ordinary hour and cannot say why, and you stop needing to say why.

This energy still wants an outlet. But it stops trying to fix the world to quiet its own ache, because the ache is quiet now. So it gives differently. It works with the grain of things instead of against it. It notices where another person's flow is stuck and helps it move, without crowding, without taking over. Vitality knows vitality on sight. And the strange arithmetic holds every time: the more of it you spend on someone else, the more of it you have. The fuel grows by burning.
siddhi:
There is a kind of seeking that refuses to be answered. It detonates. The energy that spent a life looking outward has burrowed so deep it lets go of its own center, and there is no longer a self standing in the middle of the experience collecting it. The lake stops being stirred. Nothing is reaching for anything.

What fills that stillness is bliss. Not a feeling that comes and goes with good news, but a steady current welling up from inside the body, breaking and breaking like quiet surf. The eyes go soft and unfixed. The heart runs over for no creature in particular and every creature at once.

Look back from here and the long dissatisfaction reads differently. It was never the enemy of joy. It was joy in seed form, pressing, aching, pointing the only way it knew how. The itch and the bliss were the same energy the whole time. One was the seed in the dark. The other is the flower it was always folded inside.
